svg.text: Master End-to-End Flow — All 8 Phases
PHASE 1 — User Registration
1. User installs app → POST /register {phone_number, name}
2. User Service creates user record in PostgreSQL
3. JWT token returned to client
PHASE 2 — Login + WebSocket Establishment
4. POST /login {phone, OTP}
5. User Service validates OTP → returns JWT
6. Client sends HTTP Upgrade request to WebSocket Gateway with JWT
7. Gateway validates JWT → upgrades to WebSocket
8. Chat Server: HSET ws_registry {user_id → server_id, conn_id}
9. Chat Server queries Cassandra for PENDING messages
10. Pending messages pushed to client via WebSocket
11. Client sends DELIVERY_ACK → Cassandra updated → sender gets double tick
Steps 4-11 also run automatically on every later reconnect, not just first login.
PHASE 3 — Sending a Message (Online Recipient)
12. User types → WS SEND {chat_id, content, msg_type}
13. Chat Server persists to Cassandra, status = PENDING
14. Chat Server looks up recipient in ws_registry
15. Recipient ONLINE → XADD to Redis Stream of recipient's server
16. Sender gets single tick
17. Recipient's Chat Server reads stream → pushes via WebSocket
18. Recipient sends DELIVERY_ACK → 19. Cassandra updated status=DELIVERED → 20. Sender gets double tick
PHASE 4 — Sending a Message (Offline Recipient)
21. Same send as step 12 22. Recipient NOT in ws_registry
23. INSERT to Cassandra, status = PENDING 24. Sender gets single tick
25. Notification Service triggers FCM/APNs push
26. When recipient reconnects → steps 4-11 handle delivery
PHASE 5 — Sending Media
27. User selects image → HTTP POST /media/upload to Media Service
28. Media Service uploads to S3 → returns media_url
29. Client sends WS SEND {msg_type: IMAGE, content: media_url}
30. Flow continues same as steps 13-20 31. Recipient fetches image from CloudFront CDN, not S3 directly
PHASE 6 — Group Message
32. WS SEND {group_id, content} 33. Chat Service calls Group Service → get all member user_ids
34. For each member: check ws_registry online/offline
35. Online members: push via Redis Streams → their Chat Server → WebSocket
36. Offline members: persist to Cassandra + FCM push 37. Per-member delivery tracked in group_message_delivery table
PHASE 7 — Read Receipt
38. Recipient opens chat → READ_ACK sent via WebSocket
39. Chat Server updates Cassandra: status = READ
40. Sender's Chat Server notified via Redis Streams → sender gets blue tick
PHASE 8 — Presence / Last Seen
41. WebSocket registry entry TTL = 60s, heartbeat every 30s refreshes it
42. User closes app → heartbeat stops → TTL expires after 60s
43. Redis keyspace expiry event fires 44. User Management Service: UPDATE users SET last_seen = NOW()
45. PUBLISH presence:offline → contacts with open chats see "last seen X"
This 45-step flow is the complete story: any single feature discussed in this system
(text send, offline delivery, media, groups, read receipts, presence) maps to one of these 8 phases.
P99 delivery < 100ms | ~700K msg/sec peak | at-least-once delivery + client dedup = exactly-once UX
Cassandra is written BEFORE any ACK is sent — every phase's durability rests on that one guarantee.
Chat System Design — Master End-to-End Flow
